purpose: derive the bank service operations from the integration material

notes: The pack says an IVR integration document exists (sources/documents, section 6), but it is not in the material I was given. So I used the fallback rule: every service is POST, the path is the service name with dots turned into slashes (cards.list -> /cards/list, and so on), and the body is JSON. Field names come from the test data: customerNo, cardNumber, newStatementWeek. If the integration document defines other paths, methods, field names or headers, the document wins and this description must be corrected.
No auth or channel headers appear in the material I was given, so auth_headers and every per-operation headers object are empty.
The call variable is customerNumber, but the test data names the customer field customerNo (casing kept). I used customerNo as the body field and fill it from customerNumber.

In the test data, card services (cards.balance, statement.week.get, statement.week.decide, statement.week.change) are keyed by the masked card number from cards.list (for example "540000******1234"). cardNumber must be sent exactly as cards.list returns it. Do not send the differently masked "5400********1234" that cards.balance returns.

statement.week.decide and statement.week.change have a second key, newStatementWeek. In the test data that key is the string "2", "3" or "4", while statement.week.get returns statementWeek as an integer (1). I typed newStatementWeek as an integer. The mock should match on its string form.

In the test data, contact.email.get and statement.pdf.send are keyed only by customer, not by card, so their bodies hold only customerNo. The material I was given shows no card or e-mail field for statement.pdf.send.

The test-data description says each entry has 'yanit' (body), 'http' (status) and an optional 'gecikmeSaniye' (delay in seconds). The entries themselves use 'response' instead of 'yanit'. The mock returns the content of 'response' as the body, with status 'http', after waiting 'gecikmeSaniye' seconds when that field is present.

I only had the first 14000 characters of test-customers.json, and only for customer 90000001, so every response listed here is HTTP 200. Other customers in the full file probably have error, no-card, no-debt, no-e-mail and delayed responses (other HTTP statuses, returnCode/exitState values). Those have to be copied verbatim from test-customers.json into the mock and added to this description.

In cards.list, both 540000******4253 and 545000******4253 belong to customer 92030487 and share the last 4 digits and the product name. The flow drawing says that in this case the assistant asks for the last 6 digits.
